title: Ranked runoff onboarding notes: tagging, tie-breaks, and regression triage
summary: Working notes from a ranked-runoff style bakeoff used to onboard three candidate model versions (v3.1, v3.2-quant, v3.0-pt) against our canonical prompt suites. Focus: improve median instruction-following quality without regressing cost and tail latency. This doc captures scoring heuristics, a compact win/loss snapshot, the tie-breaker policy we experimented with, and recommended follow-ups for the gating decision.
background: Context: Applied ML intake for Hosted API flagged three candidate uploads from the model-custodian pipeline. These models differ by fine-tune checkpoint and quantization path. Prior runs showed close aggregate metrics; however, there were a few edge cohorts where v3.0-pt outperformed newer candidates. Given limited rollout slots for Dedicated, we ran a ranked-runoff evaluation to surface head-to-head tradeoffs and to stress tie-break logic.
methodology: Prompt suites: instr-robustness-v3 (2.5k items), multi-turn-sim-1k (dialog), legal-summaries-lite-400 (domain-specific), regen-stability-200 (flaky responses). Metrics: human-rated usefulness (3-point rubric), automated factuality proxy (FACTOR score), median latency (99th percentile token latency measured on c6g-x instances), and cost estimate (tokens * cost-per-token profile). Scoring: primary rank = weighted score (Human 0.5, FACTOR 0.2, latency 0.2, cost 0.1). Pairwise comparisons computed via head-to-head win counts across prompts. Run notes: temperature fixed at 0.0 for classification-style prompts, 0.7 for creative prompts; same decoding seeds.
results_snapshot:
Overall weighted score (higher better):
- v3.2-quant: 0.742
- v3.1: 0.730
- v3.0-pt: 0.721

Head-to-head win counts (wins / total comparisons):
- v3.2-quant vs v3.1: v3.2-quant 1284 / 2500, v3.1 1216 / 2500 (v3.2-quant +68)
- v3.2-quant vs v3.0-pt: v3.2-quant 1320 / 2500, v3.0-pt 1180 / 2500 (v3.2-quant +140)
- v3.1 vs v3.0-pt: v3.1 1250 / 2500, v3.0-pt 1250 / 2500 (tie)

Cohort-level notes: instr-robustness-v3: v3.2-quant slightly better on hallucination reduction; multi-turn-sim: v3.1 better coherence; legal-summaries-lite: v3.0-pt has the highest precise-citation rate but at higher latency.

Performance/cost tradeoffs (median across suites):
- v3.2-quant: median latency 22ms/token, 99th 82ms, est cost 0.77x baseline
- v3.1: median latency 26ms/token, 99th 95ms, est cost 1.00x baseline
- v3.0-pt: median latency 30ms/token, 99th 130ms, est cost 1.35x baseline

Regression flags (prompts with >20 point drop in human score vs baseline):
- 17 prompts in regen-stability-200 where v3.2-quant produced truncated answers (frequent EOS).
- 9 prompts in multi-turn-sim where v3.2-quant lost context on long stateful chains.
- v3.0-pt shows 3 out-of-domain hallucination spikes on legal-summaries (investigate data overlap).
tie_breaker_policy: We trialed a two-stage tie-breaker: first, prefer lower cost when weighted-score diff < 0.01 and head-to-head within ±1% (promotes quantized models); second, prefer lower 99th latency if cost within 5%. If still tied, escalate to human adjudication on a 100-sample stratified set. Applied to the observed ties: v3.1 vs v3.0-pt resolved to v3.1 due to 0.35x better tail latency after cost parity check.
decision: Provisional recommendation: Promote v3.2-quant to a canary ring (5% traffic on Hosted API) with a restrictive route for multi-turn-heavy endpoints disabled by default. Reasoning: highest weighted score and cost upside. Caveats: address truncated-response regression and multi-turn context loss before wider rollout. Keep v3.1 in reserve as fallback for multi-turn routes; v3.0-pt should not be promoted due to high latency and cost despite domain precision in legal prompts.
